title: Deli Sandwiches and Pack-Ahead Tips
description: Work-lunch deli sandwich builds and tips for packing them ahead.

ingredients.note: or a pretzel bun if extra

steps: Pack the night before (or 2 days max ahead). Beyond that the bread gets soggy.
Spread Duke's edge to edge on both slices of bread. The mayo acts as a moisture barrier.
Cheese next to the bread on both sides, meat in the middle. Mustard goes between the meat and cheese, not right on the bread.
Candied jalapenos: pack in a small container and add at lunch, or blot them dry on a paper towel before adding.
Wrap tightly in plastic wrap or foil, then a bag. Keep cold: fridge at work, or an ice pack in a lunch bag.
source: Joe's Meal Pack, Oct 20 to Nov 4, 2026 (built by Thrifty, now kept by Meal Plan), R19
notes:
Build ideas:
- Spicy turkey: turkey, habanero jack slices, Duke's, spicy brown mustard, candied jalapenos.
- Italian-ish: salami, pepperoni, provolone, Duke's, a little spicy brown mustard.
- Turkey and provolone: turkey, provolone, Duke's, honey mustard.
- The stack: turkey, salami, pepperoni, habanero jack, Duke's, spicy brown mustard, candied jalapenos.
- Hot version (if there's a microwave at work): salami and pepperoni with provolone, 20 to 30 sec to melt.
Add a side: a handful of Utz Pub Mix or Santitas chips.
Open one lunchmeat pack at a time. Opened packs: 3 to 5 days. Smells off or slimy, toss it.
Deli sandwiches are for work lunches only.

healthy: Easy to pack ahead for a portion-sized lunch.
not_healthy: Deli meats, pepperoni and salami are processed and high in sodium.
Salami, pepperoni, cheese and mayo add saturated fat.
